narrative:
The model predicts an 88% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability means the system sees strong signs that you are likely to depart in the near future.

Three factors stood out most in driving this prediction. First, your overall years of experience pushed the decision toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have only 1-5 years of total experience, your 6-10 years places you in a group that tends to explore new opportunities. Second, having received other job offers while at the company was a major influence pulling the prediction toward leaving. Most employees the model expects to stay have not received such external offers. Third, the relatively short time you have spent in your current role (1-5 years) also contributed to the decision to predict you will leave, as longer tenure in one organization is more common among those expected to remain.

These elements together created a clear picture for the model: someone with solid experience who is already attracting interest from elsewhere and has not yet built deep roots here.

Your organization should discuss retention strategies with you, such as clearer promotion paths or better rewards. You may want to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your goals or if exploring those other opportunities makes sense. Addressing these points openly could change the outlook.
